A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VIST and provide complete, matchable text, equations, tables, and figures. Neither contains an appendix; both end with references.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original language-modeling, in-context learning, question-answering, and ablation results, including Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and adds a fast-path-only question-answering configuration in Table 3.

M1.justification: The frozen vision encoder, Resampler, cross-attention integration, PVE objective, and masking procedure are retained. The joint-training sentence adds implementation documentation; fast-path-only QA tests a configuration of the existing model.

E1.justification: The RedPajama training coverage, five language-modeling datasets, eleven in-context learning datasets, and three QA datasets remain unchanged. The added experiment changes passage routing within retained QA tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments. Table 3 retains TinyLlama and CEPE*; its additional row is a VIST configuration.

E3.justification: Section 4.4 adds an evaluation configuration sending the top ten retrieved passages through the vision encoder, with none supplied directly as text passages to the LLM (k_e=10, k_d=0). It retains the existing QA datasets and exact-match metric.

E4.justification: The new fast-path-only ablation tests whether the visual path can carry all retrieved context without direct text passages. Existing masking, token-count, context-length, backbone, and semantic-distance analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report in-context learning averages over seeds 42, 43, and 44. No new repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds exact-match scores of 21.27 on TriviaQA, 8.51 on NQ, and 10.67 on PopQA for k_e=10, k_d=0. These are new configuration results; existing numerical entries and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3), including the PVE loss and token-importance formula, are unchanged. The new proximity–relevance statement is an informal rationale, without new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and performance claims, including 2.3× token compression, 16% fewer FLOPs, and 50% less memory.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 explicitly states the assumption that proximity correlates with relevance. Section 4.4 interprets the new fast-path-only results as evidence that visual compression preserves critical contextual information.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly describes joint Resampler and LLM cross-attention training, discloses input truncation for the retained k_d=10 QA comparison, and replaces the future code-release promise with a project repository address. These disclosures do not establish changes to the earlier training or truncation procedures.

R1.justification: The same 73 cited works and research positioning are retained. Expanding the Qwen reference's author list and changing citation-range formatting are bibliographic presentation edits.

P1.justification: v4 adds limited explanatory prose and an acknowledgement, updates author affiliations and contribution notes, and adjusts capitalization. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains one configuration row, and Figure 2 moves from PDF page 3 to page 4, accompanied by text and float reflow. The embedded figure graphics are identical across versions.

improvement.justification: The added Table 3 ablation provides targeted evidence about the visual path's ability to retain context. Clearer training, routing, and truncation descriptions modestly improve experimental transparency, while the central method and principal results remain unchanged.
